return_B.why_selected:
This verdict is my own source review of the retained receipts. No TypeSafe inference results were supplied or used, and no provider judgment is retained. In this revision c5 Prometheus replaces c8 restic as a winner. The refuters showed that the native-usage matches credited to the Collector were read out of Prometheus. They also showed that the only receipt for restic, the backup tool, covers no state this layer owns. The three winners together form the telemetry path that was actually run natively, so the weakest class in the set is native_proven.

(1) c14, OpenTelemetry Collector contrib v0.161.0. observability/receipt.json records `otelcol-contrib validate` exit 0. Real native Codex 0.155.1 and Claude 2.1.278 runs of fixtures/observability-check.json exited 0 with the correct answer (lines 163-202). For Codex, collected_turn_histogram_matches_native_usage is true (line 182). For Claude, collected_request_logs_and_metrics_match is true (line 201). Six services were active, and the privacy canary recorded forbidden_marker_absent true (line 327). observability/followup-receipt.json records one fresh native SDK task run through blueprints/us-equities/workers/native_worker.py. After an analytics configuration fix, its turn histogram matched all six usage categories (total 40518; lines 97-110).

(2) c5, Prometheus. The Codex usage match was queried from the Prometheus API. observability/README.md lines 109-111 query ecosystem_codex_turn_token_usage_sum at 127.0.0.1:19090. The follow-up SDK histogram was also a Prometheus query: HTTP 200, and a retained last_over_time query returned the same values (followup-receipt.json lines 98-125). observability/backends/receipt.json records all 7 scrape targets up, readiness HTTP 200, and prometheus_historical_sample true after one restart (lines 76-97).

(3) c6, Loki v3.7.8. Claude request logs are read from Loki (README lines 112-113). The follow-up Loki query summed SDK receipts per receipt_id over 6h and returned 121288. That equals the 80770 from two earlier runs plus 40518 from the fresh run, and the fresh run published its own receipt automatically (followup-receipt.json lines 204-224). The earlier 80770 came from imported summaries of two completed runs, not new model calls. It was unchanged after a Collector restart (receipt.json lines 248-252). Loki log persistence after a backend restart was shown with a synthetic fixture only (backends/receipt.json lines 87-91).

Correction to the earlier proposal: no receipt shows a failed attempt stored in Loki. retained_failed_attempts (receipt.json lines 370-375) is the acceptance author's own process history. Three of its entries are corrections and one is an unresolved negative result (line 373). Writing a failed-status record is shown only by the offline unit test in tests/test_observability.py (lines 32-54). The live unknown-usage query returned no data, and the follow-up receipt says a receipt-based view cannot identify tasks that never emitted a receipt (followup-receipt.json lines 24 and 214-218). Restic is kept as a conditional alternative; see alternatives.

alternatives.name: restic
alternatives.why_not_default: Restic is the only candidate with a native backup and restore receipt, so it remains the preferred backup tool for this layer's backup scope term. blueprints/us-equities/hosting/backup/receipt.json records: signed checksums verified; init, backup, check --read-data ('no errors were found') and restore --verify all exit 0; 22 files and 160642 bytes restored; sha256 ok_lines 22; the independent byte comparison matched. The receipt covers only 22 static public reference files, with live_databases 0 (line 36). It states that no live SQLite, Qdrant, Loki, Prometheus, broker/order journal or transcript backup was attempted (line 125). There is no off-host destination (line 118), separate_key_escrow is not_configured, the retention step was a dry run with 0 deletions, and the timer and service are not enabled. Restic therefore has no evidence of recovering this layer's state, which is why it is not a winner.

alternatives.name: Grafana
alternatives.why_not_default: Readiness HTTP 200 is recorded. Provisioned dashboards and datasources survived a restart. agent-browser rendered the dashboard, and the follow-up render shows the SDK total of 121288. Grafana is only a view over Prometheus and Loki data; it neither collects nor retains telemetry itself. grafana_tag_build_commit_equal is false. The backends receipt contains no dashboard UI acceptance, and the first screenshot predates the SDK panel.

return_B.overturn_when:
Revise the verdict if any of the three checks below gives a different result. The existing tests/test_observability.py and tests/test_observability_backends_alerts.py are offline guards only; they cover identity, no-overwrite, the failed-status writer, the dashboard query and alert/config syntax. On their own they cannot overturn or confirm this verdict.

(1) Native re-run. Run `python3 blueprints/us-equities/workers/native_worker.py run` with the argument shape recorded at observability/followup-receipt.json line 61 (native binary, home, workspace, receipt, prompt derived from fixtures/observability-check.json, --observation-dir). Then query the Prometheus series ecosystem_codex_turn_token_usage_sum and the Loki per-receipt_id sum. The winners are overturned if the collected usage no longer equals native usage. A second run should force a failure, for example with a very short --turn-deadline-seconds. If Loki never shows its record with usage_status other than reported, failed-attempt telemetry retention stays unproven for c6 and the set must be re-judged.

(2) `python3 observability/backends/check_persistence.py --evidence-dir <fresh directory> --grafana-env <grafana env file>` (arguments as used in tests/test_observability.py lines 83-84). The Prometheus/Loki retention claim fails if a fresh run no longer records prometheus_historical_sample and loki_log true after a restart.

(3) Recovery. Promote c8 restic to a winner if a backup receipt shows check --read-data and restore --verify exit 0 with byte-identical hashes for the live Loki, Prometheus and SQLite data and the broker journal, preferably to an off-host destination. The comparison point is blueprints/us-equities/hosting/backup/receipt.json. The offline refusal cases in tests/test_offhost_restore.py are a precondition, not such a receipt.

A sandbox candidate enters the winners only after a receipt shows both network denial and research workers denied broker execution authority.
open_gaps: Failed-attempt telemetry retention is not established. No failed or unknown-usage record was observed in Loki: the 6h unknown-usage query returned no data. Only the offline unit test of the writer creates a failed-status observation, and tasks that never emit a receipt are invisible.

Recoverable state is shown only as same-host restart persistence of the observability backends, and the Loki check used a synthetic fixture. Restic backed up 22 static files, with live_databases 0, no off-host destination, no key escrow, a dry-run retention step, and timer and service not enabled.
The earlier 80770 SDK total came from imported summaries of two completed runs. Only the follow-up task (40518) published its own receipt automatically, and it is a single run.

The Loki and Collector restart checks cover one controlled restart. There is no loss/recovery acceptance under a full disk or an extended backend outage, and the receipt spool has no automatic expiry.
Traces are disabled and no trace database was deployed.

Process supervision rests on systemd is-active checks and one local Alertmanager target-down route. There is no external notification delivery or high availability, and the Dagu HTTP 401 shows only anonymous protection.
No receipt shows research workers denied broker execution authority. Sandbox network denial was configured but not exercised.
The Desktop parent export was not observed: its correlated OTel records were 0, and it was not restarted.
The existing tests under tests/ for this layer are offline guards. No named repository test measures the native-usage match or restart totals.

packet.title: Observability and hosting
packet.requirement: Run bounded research with native identity and complete returned results; supervise owned processes; retain scoped telemetry, failed attempts and recoverable state without granting research workers broker execution authority.
limitations: Native worker success and telemetry matching are bounded by the recorded task, process and account. They do not establish every native client/session, whole-task savings or unlimited allowance.
Dagu's older completed-history restart is not in-flight recovery. Later recovery receipts must be evaluated for their own process, host and workload rather than promoting all workflows.
Gateway transport health, routed text and ACP research acceptance do not establish native hook/tool parity or independent provider/model attestation.
Same-host recovery and configured restrictions do not establish off-host disaster recovery, a VM boundary, unattended broker operation or paid hosting.
